scope: Fifth-order Frontier-Science deductions from the unchanged EdgeBench v1 experiment definition, public 51-task per-time score table, and runtime-configurable LLM judge path. Proposed treatments are not EdgeBench empirical results.
source_facts: The main EdgeBench experiment schedules three independent 12-hour trials for each task-model pair and reports the same trajectories at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 hours.
The public 51-task README table contains per-time values for five models; recomputation finds that the displayed best-model sets at 2 hours and 12 hours are disjoint on 19 of 51 tasks.
EdgeBench defines an effective submission as one that sets a new best-so-far score, while the agent chooses when to submit; this is therefore an endogenous request-and-quality statistic.

The 1M-context Opus comparison leads the 200k condition by 5.8 points at 2 hours and 4.4 points at 12 hours, establishing a performance-level advantage but not by itself a larger baseline-adjusted learning slope.
The public college_english_exam_bank contract invokes grade_with_codex.py and the SForge documentation configures its grader model through the runtime SFORGE_JUDGE_MODEL environment variable.
The current TaskSpec judge-image hash does not include runtime judge_extra_env, and the persisted effective run_config.json does not record judge_extra_env.

descriptive_recomputation.source: official GitHub README public 51-task per-time table
descriptive_recomputation.tie_policy: For each checkpoint, retain the set of all models tied at the displayed maximum; count a task only when the 2h and 12h sets are disjoint.
descriptive_recomputation.interpretation: Horizon-conditioned ranking drift in displayed public scores; not a randomized causal effect of disclosed horizon.

sle_experiments.design: Randomize true disclosed 2h, 6h and 12h horizons on matched task worlds; compare independent short-run endpoints with matched prefixes from 12h-aware runs and add a preregistered random-censoring arm whose distribution, but not realized cutoff, is disclosed.

Pin a complete judge manifest and repeatedly score blinded expert anchors, exact duplicates and content-preserving style or verbosity twins across independent judge manifests, deterministic executable outcomes and expert adjudication.

At equal total trusted-feedback and confirmation budgets compare agent-requested, fixed-grid, random, cost-aware value-of-information and end-only feedback policies; require a signed prediction and action threshold before each on-demand request.

claim_boundary: No new EdgeBench performance result is claimed.
The 19-of-51 recomputation is descriptive and does not establish that horizon knowledge causes the ranking changes.
The runtime judge provenance finding does not establish that any reported EdgeBench score changed or is incorrect.
Until HZ1 is run, long-run prefixes should not be described as counterfactual short-horizon scientific policies.
Until J1 is passed, rubric or model-judge outcomes should be labeled judge-specific and should not be the sole basis for a scientific discovery claim.
Until F9 is run, effective-submission rate should not be interpreted as calibrated scientific feedback-acquisition efficiency.
